name: Illhveli, Stökkull
body:
STÖKKULL
CR 8

This massive round-bodied whale has a thick blunt head like a battering ram. Its gray hide lightens toward the belly and drooping skin flaps sag over its eyes.

XP 4,800
NE Huge outsider (aquatic, evil, illhveli, native)
Init +6; Senses blindsight 120 ft. (underwater only), darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +14

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 10, flat-footed 19 (+2 Dex, +11 natural, –2 size)
hp 103 (9d10+54)
Fort +11, Ref +8, Will +10
DR 5/good; Immune cold, pressure damage from deep water; Resist electricity 10, sonic 10
Weaknesses blinder flaps

OFFENSE

Speed swim 80 ft.
Melee bite +15 (2d6+12) or slam +15 (1d8+12)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks capsize, leaping charge, powerful charge (slam, 2d8+12), ship smasher

STATISTICS

Str 27, Dex 15, Con 22, Int 8, Wis 15, Cha 12
Base Atk +9; CMB +19; CMD 31
Feats Cleave, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Power Attack
Skills Acrobatics +14 (+50 when jumping out of the water), Intimidate +13, Perception +14, Stealth +6, Swim +28; Racial Modifiers +28 Acrobatics when jumping out of the water
Languages Aquan, Common (can’t speak)
SQ amphibious, mighty leaper

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Blinder Flaps (Ex)

A stökkull has blinder-like flaps of skin over its eyes that hinder its vision above the water unless it’s moving swiftly enough to push these slaps back. If a stökkull moves less than 40 feet on its turn, it treats all creatures and objects above the water’s surface as having concealment from it. Against underwater foes, the stökkull relies on its blindsight instead.

Leaping Charge (Ex)

A stökkull can jump out of the water as part of a charge, even if doing so requires this charge to angle vertically rather than moving directly toward the target. This combines a long jump and high jump allowing the stökkull to reach a vertical height equal to one-quarter of the horizontal distance at the midpoint of the jump. If the stökkull reaches its target and charge hits, the attack deals additional damage equal to the result of the Acrobatics check divided by 5.

Mighty Leaper (Ex)

A stökkull adds its Strength modifier on Acrobatics checks made to jump.

Ship Smasher (Su)

When a stökkull deals damage to an object with its slam attack, it ignores the first 5 points of that object’s hardness.

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Churn Water (Ex)

As a full-round action, a sverðhvalur moves up to its speed while thrashing the area of water it passes through as well as any area within its normal reach (usually 15 feet).

Creatures of Huge size or smaller in the area take 3d6+12 points of bludgeoning damage (DC 23 Reflex half ). This water becomes difficult terrain until the start of the sverðhvalur’s next turn.

Huge or smaller creatures must succeed at a DC 20 Swim check to move through this affected water; those failing their check are pulled 10 feet underwater. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Ship Breaker (Su)

When a sverðhvalur deals damage to an object with its gore attack, it deals an additional +2d6 damage and ignores the first 5 points of that object’s hardness.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold and temperate oceans
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

The stökkull is a vicious whale-like creature feared for its powerful leaps and ship?shattering ramming attacks. It has a snout with the power of a reinforced battering ram and an under-slung maw full of sharp teeth. One of its tactics is to surface and charge, then leap out of the water, breaching high into the air and smashing down on the deck of a smaller boat or breaking the back of a large whale.

Stökkulls have blinder-like flaps of skin covering their eyes, making it difficult for them to see above the surface. Sailors claim that in the distant past the stökkull’s depredations were much worse. However, a goodly priest beseeched their deity who cast down a divine curse, causing the skin flaps to grow and hindering the stökkull’s capacity to do evil.

It is said that if a stökkull is sighted in the distance, throwing a barrel, buoy, or clothing overboard may distract the creature into attacking these decoys. On bright days, a crew may sail in the direction of the sun, relying on the dazzling glare to obscure their vessel from the stökkull’s limited vision.

The sverðhvalur is a swift, aggressive illhveli driven to destroy humanoids and benign whales alike. It takes sadistic pleasure in the carnage and destruction. The illhveli’s bladed dorsal fin is a brutal weapon; the sverðhvalur swims beneath whales and slices open their bellies with crisscross slashes. Whales fear this and some beach themselves rather than face a sverðhvalur’s attack.

Wasteful by nature, the sverðhvalur eats only the tongues of its cetacean prey, leaving the rest to rot. The sverðhvalur is often shadowed by smaller marine creatures who feed on the scraps. The sverðhvalur’s dorsal blade can also punch holes in hulls or even shear cleanly through smaller vessels and can do the same to the ship’s crew.
